Compliance Answer: Simplified due diligence can be applied in low-risk cases as per the revised guidance note on FIC Act implementation, which allows for less information to be obtained and scrutiny when abuse risks are lower.
2. Relevant Regulatory Basis: Source 1 (Revised-Guidance-Note-7A–Implementation of various aspects of the Financial Crime Act) – Chunk 11067, as it explicitly mentions simplified due diligence for low abuse risk cases and outlines conditions under which less information can be obtained.
3. Explanation: The guidance note specifies that an accountable institution may apply simplified due diligence when the assessment of lower risks allows for reduced scrutiny, as long as there are justifiable grounds to ensure a balanced approach in each case (Chunk 58-60).

Human Review Required: Yes, because institutions must document their systems and controls decisions regarding ML/TF risk management within the RMCP, implying that human oversight is necessary for proper documentation and justification of simplified due diligence applications in low-risk cases (Chunk 60).
